survey: A small two-storey stone house with a round stone tower joined at its front-left corner, seen in three-quarter view from the front-left, standing on grass. The house has a purple tiled gable roof facing the camera, with a rounded ridge cap at the front and a round cross-mullioned window in the gable. A stone band runs around the house between the floors. The upper floor has two front windows and one on the right side wall. The ground floor has a plank door with a knob, a front window and a side window. The building sits on a stone plinth that runs under both the house and the tower, and a single stone step in front of the door rests on the grass. The tower has two windows and a conical purple tiled roof with a ball finial. Its eave overhangs the tower wall, and the house's left roof slope passes in front of it, which works because the tower sits slightly behind the house. A stone chimney rises from the right roof slope near the ridge, but partway up it jogs and leans to the left before its capped top. The full moon behind is part of the background. Every part rests on or joins a supporting part. Nothing floats, the counts make sense and the door and windows sit within the walls.

errors.where: Chimney on the right roof slope, upper half
errors.what: The chimney shaft bends: the lower section rises straight out of the roof, then the upper section kinks and leans left with its bricks out of line. A masonry chimney this thin could not hold up an off-balance top section, so it reads as a bent tube rather than stacked brick. This could pass as cartoon whimsy, but it is still the only structurally questionable part.

fix: Make the brick chimney straight and vertical, rising plumb from the right roof slope with evenly stacked bricks and a flat stone cap on top. No bend or lean.
